must_fix.title: With shadowDOM on, a target slotted into a web component gets hidden: the wrapper around its <slot> receives aria-hidden
must_fix.evidence:
The walker now enters shadow roots via createShadowTreeWalker, and nodeContains(wrapper, slottedTarget) is false, so the wrapper element containing the is hidden; in the rendered tree the slotted target sits inside it. Probe (enableShadowDOM(); host shadow '
', input target as host light child; ariaHideOutside([target])): this change logs 'wrap true slot null header true host null other true'; the same probe against the HEAD version of ariaHideOutside.ts logs 'wrap null slot null header null host null other true'. Contradicts 'The hosts on the path to a target stay visible' and regresses behavior with the flag on. No test covers slotted targets.

report:
I wouldn't merge this yet. The change itself is mostly sound, but with shadow DOM support on it now hides targets that are slotted into a web component. **Checks:** all pass. - `yarn jest packages/@react-aria/overlays`: 10 suites, 201 tests passed. - `yarn eslint packages/@react-aria/overlays`: exit 0. - `yarn check-types`: exit 0. - `node scripts/lint-packages.js` and `yarn constraints`: no output. - The new `@react-stately/flags` dependency matches what sibling packages declare (`@react-aria/interactions`, `@react-aria/utils`, `@react-aria/table` all use `^3.1.2`), and `yarn.lock` is consistent with it. **Must fix — a target slotted into a web component gets hidden.** With shadow DOM support on, the tree walker now enters the shadow root of every host it skips. In that shadow root, the wrapper element that holds the `` doesn't count as containing the slotted target, so the wrapper gets `aria-hidden="true"`. In the rendered tree the target sits inside that wrapper, so screen readers lose the trigger or dialog itself. This happens whenever a target is a light-DOM child of a custom element that wraps its slot, like a layout or card component, which is a common pattern. The issue says "the hosts on the path to a target stay visible", and the slot wrapper is on that path. I reproduced it with a temporary probe in `packages/@react-aria/overlays/test/`, since deleted. The probe sets up host → shadow root `
`, puts `target` (an input) as the host's light-DOM child, calls `enableShadowDOM()` and then `ariaHideOutside([target])`: - **With this change:** `wrap true slot null header true host null other true`, so the wrapper around the slot is hidden and the target with it. - **Same probe against the `HEAD` version of `ariaHideOutside.ts`, flag on:** `wrap null slot null header null host null other true`, so the target stayed visible before. None of the new tests cover a slotted target. The fix should come with one. **Other edge cases I tried, all fine:** - A `root` option inside a shadow root. - A shadow host added later to the light DOM. - A target that is itself a shadow host, with content added to its shadow root later. - A shadow host inside a `role="row"`. `git status` is back to exactly the four modified files the PR started with. ```json {"mergeable": false, "must_fix": [{"title": "With shadowDOM on, a target slotted into a web component gets hidden: the wrapper around its receives aria-hidden", "kind": "regression", "evidence": "The walker now enters shadow roots via createShadowTreeWalker, and nodeContains(wrapper, slottedTarget) is false, so the wrapper element containing the is hidden; in the rendered tree the slotted target sits inside it. Probe (enableShadowDOM(); host shadow '
', input target as host light child; ariaHideOutside([target])): this change logs 'wrap true slot null header true host null other true'; the same probe against the HEAD version of ariaHideOutside.ts logs 'wrap null slot null header null host null other true'. Contradicts 'The hosts on the path to a target stay visible' and regresses behavior with the flag on. No test covers slotted targets."}], "nits": []} ```
